Project Results and Discussion: Task 1: Validation of TCCs as efficient gas-barriers Task Summary: To develop TCCs (conductive media + polymer) with appropriate gas- barrier and optoelectronic properties for the prolonged operation of PSCs, relevant parameters such as WVTR, electrical conductivity, and optical transparency were benchmarked before and after exposure to aging conditions. Subtask 1.1: Polymers water vapor (WVTR), and oxygen (OTR) transmission rate benchmarking: WVTRs of solvent-free, room-temperature curable polyepoxies were measured using NREL's established techniques before and after 1,000 hours of damp heat (45°C, 85% R.H.) aging. The facilities required for OTR testing were to be established at NREL; however, this was not completed within the project period. Subtask Summary: In the early stages of this project, three polymer candidates were considered for the polymer matrix, including 1) a bisphenol -A based aromatic epoxy resin (Aluzine brand) with high optical clarity and environmental resistance, 2) Masterbond EP21LSCL-2 aliphatic epoxy with superb optical clarity, excellent non-yellowing characteristics and resistance to outdoor environments, and 3) thermoplastic ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA) which accompany a large body of research for use in PV applications.
